content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in the short term, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes often precede sharp price drops, indicating model lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals.", "Models show mean-reversion bias when prices fall below historical averages, but fail to anticipate extreme lows.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish, suggesting sentiment amplifies model error.", "Models exhibit significant overshoot during bullish sentiment phases, leading to overconfident price peaks.", "Sentiment history with multiple 1.00 values correlates with forecast divergence, suggesting sentiment overrides model calibration.", "Forecast bias is strongest in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, indicating delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.", "Models underperform when sentiment is mixed or volatile, highlighting sensitivity to sentiment noise."]}
